motivation: FG+t Wald-type upper bounds were materially anti-conservative at the 3 pp NI, 10% FNR, and 5% FPR boundaries, especially for low event probabilities and variable cluster sizes.

two_sample_candidate.method: Newcombe MOVER risk-difference upper bound formed from the two cluster-adjusted Wilson score intervals
two_sample_candidate.important: This clustered MOVER construction is a design candidate that combines established single-clustered-proportion score intervals with the established Newcombe MOVER risk-difference construction; it must be validated empirically before any preregistration freeze.

important: The clustered-score candidate materially improved calibration relative to FG+t but still exceeded the prespecified type-I boundaries. It is rejected for confirmatory use and must not be used for power sizing.
